questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Sunny weather and different culture

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Valencia is an ideal student city, with the UPV being a really good university, both academically and socialy

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy to see orientation dates at the university, however be patient for your course registration, as the process might not be completed until a few weeks into the semester.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: No assistance but orientation at the UPV faculty

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I rented an AirBnB for the first week, to find an apartment. Ended up being a little more difficult than anticipated, but definitely possible. I think you should look for a place in Mestella, Algiros, Blaso Ibañez or the old city center. The first 3 are closer to the university and there are a lot of cheap places, but the old city center is obviously a great place to live.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Use idealista and be aware of your contract; remember it's possible to cancel your contract and move, if you're not comfortable with your living situation

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The course catalog is great for finding the right courses of your liking, but as you have to design your own timetable, you have to manually check if all your chosen courses align. I had courses in the morning, midday and evening, as it's really nice with the flexibility

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Online course registration tool

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: If you register fast, you should get pretty much all the courses you want. If you dont get a course you really want, just go to the first lecture and talk to the professor. Shouldn't be a problem

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Choose some different type of courses

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Little lower complexity than at UCPH, but a bigger workload as there are several mandatory tests throughout the semester, as well as exams in all courses in both november and january

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Less dialogue with the professor, but otherwise nothing dramatically different

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. Mathematical Analysis
2. Software engineering 
3. Intelligent Systems 
4. Automata Theory and Formal Languages 
5. ESPAÑOL III GENERAL (A) B1
6. Biomedical data science

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Biomedical data science is difficult but super interesting, and the professors are really good. 
The spanish course is obviously relevant.
Software engineering is also pretty interesting, where you build a software engineering project in C#

questions.answer: Nothing. Everything is cheaper than in Denmark

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Try to find your good cheap local places

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The best part of the UPV is the wide range of sports offered. Make sure to check the dates for registering for whatever sport you like, however as long as you have the UPV sports-app, you are able to reserve sports-courts for free. I played a lot of tennis, padel and beach volley

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Do all the sports you like, and register for all the sports classes that you might find interesting

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go out for paella and beers

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Easy if you speak spanish, otherwise difficult

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Language barrier

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Relaxed atmosphere and the frequency of going out to eat

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Engage in the non-academic activities offered by the university!!
2. In doubt, go ahead
3. Make an effort to learn some spanish

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Although they say attendance is mandatory, they usually dont register it, so don't focus too much on the courses, and enjoy your stay

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Weather and sports

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Adjusting to the new routines

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Valencia is now one of my favorite cities, and I can't emphasize enough, how good a student-city it is!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
